title: Panitumumab + FOLFIRI

agents.name: Panitumumab
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth messages at the cell surface
agents.explanation: Panitumumab attaches to EGFR, a receptor on the outside of cells. This can interrupt signals that help some bowel cancers grow. A tumour RAS test helps identify whether this approach is suitable. EGFR also supports healthy skin, which explains why skin and nail changes need attention.
agents.watch: Report rash, painful cracks or nail changes early. Eye pain or blurred vision, new breathing symptoms, severe diarrhoea, or blistering skin need prompt assessment. Blood tests check minerals such as magnesium.
risks: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

agents.name: Irinotecan
agents.explanation: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about cramps, sweating or diarrhoea during the infusion. Diarrhoea starting later needs the separate written treatment and contact plan.
risks: Rare serious lung or allergic reactions

agents.name: Folinic acid
agents.explanation: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself.
agents.watch: The combined treatment can increase mouth soreness and diarrhoea. Report these promptly. Rare allergic reactions can occur.

agents.name: Fluorouracil
agents.explanation: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
agents.watch: Diarrhoea, mouth sores and skin soreness may become serious. Chest pain during the pump infusion needs emergency assessment. Unexpected severe early toxicity can occur even after DPD testing.
risks: Severe early toxicity including DPD-related toxicity

questions.q: Why do I need a RAS test?
questions.a: RAS is part of the growth-signalling pathway inside cancer cells. If it is changed by a mutation, blocking EGFR is unlikely to help. Your team needs a validated wild-type RAS result before panitumumab. Other tumour tests and the treatment aim also affect the choice.

questions.q: Is this the same as checkpoint immunotherapy?
questions.a: Panitumumab is a targeted antibody against EGFR. It works differently from checkpoint treatments used in some other cancer regimens. Ask your team which treatment class and side effects apply to you.

questions.q: Does a rash mean the treatment is working?
questions.a: A rash is a recognised drug effect, but it cannot tell you whether your cancer is responding. Report it early so it can be treated. Scans, symptoms and clinical review guide the response assessment.

questions.q: Will I need radiotherapy as part of this cycle?
questions.a: These panitumumab regimens do not contain a scheduled radiotherapy course. If radiotherapy is recommended separately, your oncology teams will explain its purpose and timing. Do not assume it occurs on infusion or pump days.

questions.q: What about pregnancy, breastfeeding or fertility?
questions.a: Discuss pregnancy plans and fertility before treatment. Panitumumab requires contraception during treatment and for two months afterwards, and breastfeeding should be avoided for that period. When chemotherapy is also included, its precautions may last longer; ask for the instructions for the whole regimen.

questions.q: Does having more side effects mean treatment is working?
questions.a: No. Side effects do not reliably show whether the cancer is responding. Report them so they can be treated. Your team assesses benefit using the tests and review plan appropriate to your cancer.

questions.q: Why might a dose be delayed or reduced?
questions.a: Your team may allow recovery, investigate a symptom or reduce the chance of lasting harm. Ask which drug changes, why, and when review is planned. A delay does not itself mean treatment has failed.

questions.q: What should I say when calling?
questions.a: Give the regimen name, last treatment date, symptoms and when they started. Explain whether you can eat, drink, pass urine and manage usual activities. Give your temperature if available, but do not delay calling to collect details.

questions.q: Which checks continue when treatment changes or finishes?
questions.a: Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last panitumumab dose. Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Escalate persistent diarrhoea, fever or dehydration between visits. Check INR if taking warfarin, as clinically indicated.

phases_title: Treatment, review and the next cycle
phases_note: There is no fixed four-cycle course. Scans, symptoms and your priorities guide continuation or changes. With combination treatment, the antibody and chemotherapy may need different holds or changes.
timeline_note: Bars show planned treatment and possible symptom patterns, not measured risk. Side effects can overlap and persist.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Act on fever, sudden illness or a new serious symptom whenever it occurs. Do not wait for the next appointment.
teachback: Can you explain which medicines you are receiving, the schedule, the contact plan and the symptoms that need prompt help?
consent_support: Discuss RAS selection, skin/nail and eye effects, electrolyte monitoring for eight weeks after completion, infusion reactions and rare serious lung/skin toxicity. Confirm DPD testing, antiemetics, atropine suitability and the separate delayed-diarrhoea plan. Explain port/PICC care and pump connection/disconnection.
urgent_extra: Report new breathing difficulty, eye pain or blurred vision, blistering or infected skin, severe diarrhoea or dehydration promptly. Also report new chest pain, fever or a line/pump problem immediately.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim and review plan
chapters.intro: Understand why this option fits your cancer.

items.title: The setting matters
items.text: Panitumumab + FOLFIRI is used for bowel cancer that has spread and has a confirmed wild-type RAS result. This NCCP regimen covers first-line treatment and selected second-line treatment after a fluoropyrimidine regimen without irinotecan. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: What the tumour tests mean
items.text: RAS wild type is required for panitumumab. Your team also considers the cancer location, other molecular results, previous treatment and whether surgery or other local treatment could be useful. A positive eligibility result is not a promise of benefit.

chapters.title: Before you start and before each cycle
chapters.intro: The team checks that the plan remains suitable.

items.title: Checks and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver function and minerals, current symptoms, allergies and all medicines. DPD testing is needed before fluorouracil unless already documented. Tell the team about severe reactions to previous chemotherapy.

items.title: Skin, eyes and breathing
items.text: Tell the team about an existing rash, skin infection, dry or painful eyes, contact lenses, or previous lung inflammation. Report new eye pain, light sensitivity or visual change promptly.

chapters.title: Living with treatment
chapters.intro: Build the plan around what matters to you.

items.title: Skin and nails
items.text: Ask for your skin-care plan before the first infusion. Use the recommended moisturiser and sun protection; your team may prescribe a cream or an antibiotic. Do not use ordinary acne treatments without advice. Avoid friction on sore skin and tell the team about painful nail folds.

items.title: Food, activity and support
items.text: Keep fluids and nourishing food within reach. Pace activity around energy levels and ask for dietetic, emotional or practical support. If symptoms prevent eating, drinking or usual tasks, contact the team.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss pregnancy plans and fertility before treatment. Panitumumab requires contraception during treatment and for two months afterwards, and breastfeeding should be avoided for that period. When chemotherapy is also included, its precautions may last longer; ask for the instructions for the whole regimen.

chapters.title: When treatment changes or finishes
chapters.intro: Follow-up continues after the last infusion.

items.title: Monitoring and recovery
items.text: Continue your skin plan and planned magnesium, calcium and potassium checks for about eight weeks after panitumumab. New symptoms still need review. Ask when to stop prescribed supportive medicines.

items.title: Treatment choices
items.text: Your team may pause, reduce, change or stop one or more medicines. Ask which medicine changes, why, and what the next review will assess. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment.

chapters.title: Recognise changes early
chapters.intro: You do not need to identify the responsible medicine before asking for help.

items.title: When to call
items.text: Report new breathing difficulty, eye pain or blurred vision, blistering or infected skin, severe diarrhoea or dehydration promptly. Also report new chest pain, fever or a line/pump problem immediately.

items.title: Track impact, not just a score
items.text: Describe when symptoms began, whether they are worsening, and whether they affect food, fluids, sleep, walking or daily tasks. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Use the passport if it helps; it is not required to access this information.

items.title: Two bowel-symptom patterns
items.text: Cramps, sweating or early diarrhoea during irinotecan need immediate nursing attention. Delayed diarrhoea begins more than 24 hours later and can occur before the next cycle. Follow your written treatment and escalation plan; fever, blood, severe pain or dehydration requires urgent assessment.

chapters.title: Visits, access and coordination
chapters.intro: Know what happens in the clinic and what happens at home.

items.title: The delivery plan
items.text: Day 1: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours; disconnection is arranged around Day 3. A cycle lasts 14 days. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable.

items.title: Radiotherapy or other treatment
items.text: This regimen has no routine radiotherapy component. If another treatment is proposed, ask whether it happens before, during or after this course and who will coordinate the appointments.

purpose: This combination aims to control bowel cancer that has spread and has a confirmed RAS wild-type result. The choice depends on previous treatment and your health.
schedule_summary: A 14-day cycle: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil start on Day 1, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours. Arrange disconnection around Day 3. Continue according to benefit and tolerance.
context_label: RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; first-line or selected second-line

phases.label: A repeating 14-day cycle
phases.detail: Day 1: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours; disconnection is arranged around Day 3. A cycle lasts 14 days. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable.

timeline.label: Delayed diarrhoea
timeline.text: Can start after 24 hours; report early

timeline.label: Blood counts / infection
timeline.text: Timing varies; no guaranteed safe days

timeline.label: Skin / nails
timeline.text: May develop or accumulate over cycles

day_groups.title: Infusion and pump connection
day_groups.body: The team reviews symptoms, blood tests including minerals and your treatment plan. Panitumumab and the day-ward chemotherapy are followed by connection of the fluorouracil pump.
day_groups.action: Before leaving, confirm the pump-care instructions, disconnection appointment and contact number.

day_groups.title: The pump is delivering treatment
day_groups.body: The pump runs for approximately 46 hours from connection. Keep it and the line secure and dry as taught. The team confirms the actual disconnection appointment.
day_groups.action: Call for a leaking, disconnected or unexpectedly stopped pump. Do not reconnect, alter settings or disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained and instructed.

day_groups.title: After disconnection
day_groups.body: Delayed diarrhoea can begin after the first 24 hours and may continue after the pump is removed. Use the written plan and contact the team early. Mouth soreness, nausea and tiredness can overlap.
day_groups.action: Report poor intake, persistent diarrhoea or mouth pain early. Chest pain or major breathing difficulty requires emergency help.

day_groups.title: Between visits and the next review
day_groups.body: Blood counts can fall between visits. Tell the team about bowel symptoms, mouth pain and how you are managing daily activities. Treatment proceeds only after review.
day_groups.action: Bring the symptom passport and check the next appointment. Day 1 usually repeats 14 days after this cycle started, only if confirmed.

support.title: Panitumumab + FOLFIRI
support.text: No routine panitumumab premedication unless previous hypersensitivity/local policy indicates. Written delayed-diarrhoea plan and urgent fever/dehydration advice; do not confuse with acute cholinergic management. Skin care and electrolytes; monthly Mg/Ca/electrolytes for two months after last panitumumab.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: For selected people whose bowel cancer had already received treatment, adding panitumumab improved tumour shrinkage and delayed progression. A longer overall survival was not established in this analysis.
evidence.interpretation: For selected people whose bowel cancer had already received treatment, adding panitumumab improved tumour shrinkage and delayed progression. A longer overall survival was not established in this analysis.
evidence.population: Prospective-retrospective RAS analysis of second-line metastatic colorectal cancer.
evidence.limitations: The NCCP also includes first-line use, but these figures apply to the second-line analysis.

chronology_notes.title: The planned treatment
chronology_notes.text: Day 1: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours; disconnection is arranged around Day 3. A cycle lasts 14 days. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable.

chronology_notes.title: Skin care continues between visits
chronology_notes.text: Rash or nail changes may build over several cycles. Report symptoms early and follow your written plan.

chronology_notes.title: Blood tests after the final dose
chronology_notes.text: Mineral checks continue for about eight weeks after panitumumab. There is no guaranteed safe day for symptoms.

anatomy: New eye pain or visual change needs prompt advice.
Report ulcers or pain affecting eating and drinking.
New chest pain or breathlessness needs urgent assessment.
Report diarrhoea, increased stoma output or severe abdominal pain.
Reduced urine, cramps or weakness need advice; keep your blood-test appointments.
Report rash, cracks or painful nails early.
Report painful redness, peeling or difficulty using your hands or walking.
Pain, leakage, swelling or a loose connection needs immediate advice.
indication_text: RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer; first-line or selected second-line
administration_text: Panitumumab is given before chemotherapy. Fluorouracil has a short dose and a separate 46-hour infusion. Irinotecan can cause an early cholinergic reaction and a different delayed-diarrhoea problem; both require an agreed plan.
monitoring_summary: Validated extended RAS wild-type result and exact first-/second-line indication; review prior irinotecan exposure. FBC, renal and liver profile; DPD test before fluorouracil. Renal impairment can confound uracil-based testing. Baseline electrolytes, magnesium and calcium; bowel function, obstruction risk, skin, lung symptoms, medication interactions and pump readiness. ECG if cardiac function is compromised. FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle. Review early and delayed diarrhoea separately, hydration, fever, mouth soreness and skin/eye/respiratory symptoms. Check magnesium/calcium/potassium and correct abnormalities according to the local EGFR monitoring plan. Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last panitumumab dose. Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Escalate persistent diarrhoea, fever or dehydration between visits. Check INR if taking warfarin, as clinically indicated.

sections.title: Treatment phases and appointments
sections.text: A 14-day cycle: panitumumab, irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil start on Day 1, followed by a fluorouracil pump for about 46 hours. Arrange disconnection around Day 3. Continue according to benefit and tolerance.

sections.title: Checks after treatment
sections.text: Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last panitumumab dose. Disease assessment follows the consultant plan. Escalate persistent diarrhoea, fever or dehydration between visits. Check INR if taking warfarin, as clinically indicated.

sections.title: Access and practical support
sections.text: Central venous access, a 46-hour fluorouracil pump, planned disconnect and emergency contacts. Provide written delayed-diarrhoea instructions separately from atropine for acute cholinergic symptoms.
